It also concedes up front that the imperfect stem vowel is not recoverable from that class and must be stored per lexeme.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: In the baseline triliteral perfect the first radical invariably carries a, so only the second-radical vowel varies and exactly three classes result.
The a-vowel class is the most frequent of the three and skews toward transitive action predicates.
The i-vowel class skews toward bodily and emotional states and toward perception predicates.
The u-vowel class denotes inherent qualities and its members are intransitive.
A verb of the a-class may take any of the three possible imperfect stem vowels, so that vowel is lexical information and cannot be computed from the perfect.
Verbs of the i-class usually take a in the imperfect and verbs of the u-class usually take u.
Every augmented pattern is a predictable semantic shift applied to the baseline sense of the same root, so the baseline must be known first.
The lesson's overview grid of the pattern series presents nine rows and silently omits the final-gemination pattern, so it cannot be used as an inventory of the series.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The pattern's only augment is gemination of the second radical; nothing is prefixed and nothing is infixed.
Its imperfect carries u on the subject prefix and i on the position before the final radical, in every person.
The pattern licenses exactly three readings: causation, intensification or repetition, and valency increase over an intransitive base.
Which of the licensed readings applies in a given occurrence is settled by context and by the lexical entry, not by the pattern itself.
The default masdar of the pattern is the تَفْعِيل family.
Verbs of foreign or quadriliteral origin that resemble this pattern belong to it and merely take a ة-final masdar.

Several entries in the lesson's derivation tables pair the augmented verb with no base verb at all or with a bare noun, so the derivation is being presented as a semantic relation rather than a formal one.

common_mistakes.pattern: Writing the imperfect with a on the subject prefix.
common_mistakes.why_wrong: This pattern fixes u on the prefix; a on the prefix belongs to other patterns and destroys the identification.
common_mistakes.correction_principle: Treat the prefix vowel as part of the pattern's identity, not as a free choice.

common_mistakes.pattern: Overlooking the gemination and reading the stem as the unaugmented baseline.
common_mistakes.why_wrong: The gemination is the only thing that distinguishes the two, so ignoring it collapses two distinct lexemes.
common_mistakes.correction_principle: Inspect the second radical for a shadda before assigning any stem label.

common_mistakes.pattern: Assuming every instance of the pattern is causative.
common_mistakes.why_wrong: The pattern licenses three readings and the causative is only the most frequent.
common_mistakes.correction_principle: Let the object and the base sense select the reading rather than defaulting to causation.

common_mistakes.pattern: Dropping the gemination when person suffixes are attached.
common_mistakes.why_wrong: The gemination is the pattern's exponent and is invariant across the paradigm.
common_mistakes.correction_principle: Preserve the geminate in every inflected cell.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The pattern's exponent is a long a inserted between the first and second radicals and it is present in every inflected cell.
The pattern implies a second participant even when no second participant is expressed in the clause.
The pattern licenses exactly three readings: mutual action, attempted or competitive action, and action directed toward someone.
The pattern has two masdar families, of which the مُفَاعَلة family is the more common and the فِعَال family clusters around struggle and combat senses.
A single lexeme may take both masdar families with a difference in nuance between act and abstract concept.
Several table rows derive a member of this pattern from a bare noun rather than from a base verb of the same root, so what is offered as a verb-to-verb shift is in part a denominal derivation.
The side-by-side contrast grid fills the cell for this pattern with a rarely attested verb purely to complete the grid, so the grid is not usable as attestation evidence.
The mutual reading entails that a transitive use of the pattern encodes the second party as its object rather than as a mere patient.

The pattern never governs a direct object and its subject is always the undergoer.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The pattern prefixes a connective hamza and infixes ت immediately after the first radical.
In the imperfect the initial hamza is lost and the subject prefix carries a with i before the final radical.
When the first radical belongs to the plain voiced coronal class, the infix is realized as a voiced coronal and the two merge.
When the first radical is one of the emphatics, the infix is realized as the emphatic coronal.
When the first radical is a semivowel of the w type, that radical is replaced by ت and geminates with the infix.
For one of the emphatic first radicals more than one output is transmitted, so the rule is not single-valued.
The pattern's default reading is self-directed and its reciprocal reading is marginal relative to the earlier تَـ plus long-vowel pattern.
Several base-verb pairings offered in the productive-verb list are etymological rather than synchronically transparent, so the base gloss cannot be used to predict the augmented sense.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The restricted pattern geminates the final radical under a connective-hamza prefix and keeps the gemination in the imperfect.
That pattern is confined to colour terms and bodily defects and cannot be extended to new meanings.
That pattern is always intransitive and inchoative: the subject comes to have the quality rather than imposing it.
The productive pattern prefixes اِسْتَـ, loses the hamza in the imperfect, and takes a on the subject prefix with i before the final radical.
The productive pattern licenses three readings: seeking or requesting, deeming or estimating, and extracting or making ready.
The productive pattern is usually transitive.

At least two items listed as members of the اِسْتَـ pattern are in fact ت-infix stems whose first radical is س, and one of them is listed as a member of the ت-infix pattern in the immediately preceding lesson, so the two lessons contradict each other on the same lexeme.
The base column of the productive pattern's derivation table contains stems belonging to other augmented patterns rather than to the baseline, so it is not a baseline-to-derived mapping.
The lesson presents the ten patterns as complete without mentioning the extended variant of the restricted pattern used for the same semantic fields.

select among the productive pattern's readings using the object and the base sense
derive the masdar from the pattern rather than from the root
conditions: the restricted pattern is available only for the two named semantic fields
the estimative reading presupposes a quality-denoting base predicate
the seeking reading presupposes a base predicate whose action can be requested of another party
exceptions: no new member of the restricted pattern may be coined even where the semantics would seem to fit
several members of the productive pattern are intransitive, contrary to the stated transitivity generalization
stems that merely begin with the same letter sequence as the productive pattern belong to a different pattern
contrasts: gemination of the final radical against gemination of the second radical
inchoative acquisition of a quality against causing that quality
a closed non-extensible pattern against a fully productive one
seeking a base action against performing it
the two masdar families against each other

common_mistakes.pattern: Confusing the final-gemination pattern with the second-radical-gemination pattern.
common_mistakes.why_wrong: The position of the gemination is the only formal difference and the two have opposite argument structures.
common_mistakes.correction_principle: Read which radical bears the shadda, then read off causative versus inchoative accordingly.

common_mistakes.pattern: Coining new members of the restricted pattern by analogy.
common_mistakes.why_wrong: The pattern is a closed class and does not extend beyond its two semantic fields.
common_mistakes.correction_principle: Use a baseline quality verb where the restricted pattern is unavailable.

common_mistakes.pattern: Using u on the imperfect subject prefix of the productive pattern.
common_mistakes.why_wrong: The connective-hamza patterns take a on the prefix.
common_mistakes.correction_principle: Group the prefix vowel by pattern class rather than by augmentation.

common_mistakes.pattern: Dropping a root hamza when forming the productive pattern from a hamza-initial root.
common_mistakes.why_wrong: That hamza is a radical and appears throughout the paradigm, unlike the pattern's own prefix hamza.
common_mistakes.correction_principle: Separate radical hamza from prefix hamza before applying the template.

Colour and defect terms link the restricted pattern to adjectival noun entries. No particle (p) relevance.

proposed_new_units.summary: A per-root and per-semantic-field admissibility gate answering whether a given root may realize a given augmented verb pattern at all: the first-radical gap set that blocks the ن-prefix pattern, and the closed semantic fields that alone license the final-gemination pattern.
proposed_new_units.why_existing_insufficient: u-s02 as catalogued enumerates and describes the pattern series; the substance here is not what a pattern looks like but whether a root is admitted to it, which is a licensing decision consumed before any template is applied. If u-s02 already carries an admissibility table rather than only form descriptions, this folds into u-s02 instead of standing alone.
